entities.summary: Józef Zabiełło h. Topór was a Polish–Lithuanian nobleman (szlachcic) of the Toppingi family, who played a crucial role in shaping the final years of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. Born in 1734, he became a member of the Lithuanian Grand Master of the Hunt from 1775, serving under Stanisław Poniatowski, and later participated in the 1793–1795 partitions of Poland. Zabiełło's loyalty to the Russian Empire led to his appointment as deputy to the Great Sejm and Field Hetman of Lithuania in 1793. His actions significantly contributed to the eventual absorption of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth into the Russian Empire. In 1794, he died in a duel, leaving behind a legacy of loyalty and treachery that continues to be debated among historians. The fall of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth marked the end of an era in Eastern Europe, and Zabiełło's role in it remains a topic of discussion among scholars.

Józef Zabiełło h. Topór was a Polish–Lithuanian nobleman (szlachcic) of Lithuanian descent, born into the nobility, and died in 1794. He was a member of the top Polish-Lithuanian aristocracy and held significant positions, including Lithuanian Grand Master of the Hunt from 1775 and Field Hetman of Lithuania from 1793. His actions as a supporter of the Russian Empire in the last years of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth had significant regional consequences.

Zabiełło was a key figure in the politics of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth during the late 18th century. His involvement in the Permanent Council and the Great Sejm demonstrates his importance in the regional politics of the time. As a supporter of the Russian Empire, he played a role in the decline of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.

Józef Zabiełło's legacy is that of a regional figure who played a significant role in the decline of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. His actions as a supporter of the Russian Empire had a lasting impact on the region, contributing to the eventual dissolution of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.

The Russian Empire's influence in the region during the late 18th century was a significant factor in the decline of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. The empire's expansion and support for regional leaders like Zabiełło weakened the Commonwealth's position and paved the way for its eventual dissolution.

The Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth's dissolution in 1795 marked the end of the region's independence and had significant consequences for the region's politics and economy. The Russian Empire's expansion into the region led to the establishment of the Russian-controlled Polish-Lithuanian territories, which would eventually become part of the Russian Empire.
